title: Hypertension and antihypertensive therapy as risk factors for type 2 diabetes mellitus
authors: Gress TW, Nieto FJ, Shahar E, Wofford MR, Brancati FL
followUp: 6 years, with fasting glucose measured at 3 and 6 years
population: Adults aged 45 to 64 years without diabetes in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities study, four US communities
funder: Supported by contracts with the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (N01-HC-55015, N01-HC-55016, N01-HC-55018, N01-HC-55019, N01-HC-55020, N01-HC-55021 and N01-HC-55022) for the ARIC collaborative study; by a National Institutes of Health training grant (T32HL07180); and by an Established Investigator grant from the American Heart Association.
result: After adjustment for age, sex, race, education, adiposity, family history of diabetes, physical activity, other health-related behaviour and coexisting illness, people with hypertension taking beta-blockers had a 28% higher risk of subsequent diabetes than people with hypertension taking no antihypertensive drug (relative hazard 1.28, 95% CI 1.04 to 1.57). Thiazide diuretics (0.91, 0.73 to 1.13), ACE inhibitors and calcium channel antagonists were not associated with greater risk.
